column1: # Free2AITools work order N -- the EXPLICIT host-IPC channel list (ruling B, b2).
# WHY A FILE AND NOT A HARDCODED SCATTER: "classified" has to be checkable. A
# regex buried in a script is not a list a reviewer can read, so the whole
# classification lives here and the scripts read it. A test asserts that no
# channel path or pattern is hardcoded in the launcher any more. The identical
# enumeration is carried in the standing offline-execution preconditions
# document so the two can be compared by hand.
# HOW IT IS USED (the strict option):
#   CLASSIFIED  -> netns-establish.sh MASKS it while still privileged. If the
#                  path EXISTS and the masking returns rc != 0, the run aborts
#                  at the ESTABLISH stage with exit 71 and phase C never starts.
#                  "Never touched" is therefore a CONSTRUCTIVE fact: no audit
#                  connect() is ever made to a live classified socket.
#                  A path that does not exist needs no masking and is recorded
#                  ABSENT -- that is also a constructive fact, not an excuse.
#   RECORD_ONLY -> enumerated and recorded at the final identity, never probed,
#                  never connected to, and never a pass/fail input.
# COLUMNS (tab separated):
#   1 CLASS     CLASSIFIED | RECORD_ONLY
#   2 MATCH     PATH (literal) | PATTERN (POSIX ERE, matched against sockets
#               discovered under the search roots)
#   3 TARGET    the literal path, or the ERE
#   4 MASK      TMPFS_DIR (empty read-only tmpfs over a directory)
#               BIND_NULL (bind /dev/null over a single socket inode)
#               NONE      (record only)
#   5 RATIONALE why this channel could act on the subtree's behalf
# SEARCH ROOTS for PATTERN discovery: /run /var/run /tmp, maxdepth 3.
# SCOPE (N3-3): only channels that can actually be present in this runner and
# this test chain. This is not a scan of every possible filesystem behaviour.
